summary_cn: 本文提出的使用SHAP量化分析和指导选择强化学习（RL）配置的方法，可用于优化金融交易策略。通过解释特定超参数对RL智能体泛化能力的影响，可以系统地提高交易模型的鲁棒性，使其在不同市场状态下保持稳定性能，从而增强策略的实际部署价值。

title: Decision Tree Learning on Product Spaces
summary: Decision tree learning has long been a central topic in theoretical computer science, driven by its practical importance. A fundamental and widely used method for decision tree construction is the top-down greedy heuristic, which recursively splits on the most influential variable. Despite its empirical success, theoretical analysis of this heuristic has been limited. A recent breakthrough by Blanc et al. (ITCS, 2020) provided the first rigorous theoretical guarantees for the greedy approach, but only under the uniform distribution. We extend this analysis to the more general and practically relevant setting of arbitrary product distributions. Our main result shows that for any function $f$ computable by an optimal decision tree of size $s$, maximum depth $D_{\text{opt}}$, and average depth $\Delta_{\text{opt}}$, the greedy heuristic constructs an $\epsilon$-approximating tree whose size grows at most with $\exp(\Delta_{\text{opt}} D_{\text{opt}} \log(e/\epsilon))$. In the special case where the optimal tree is a full binary tree, this bound improves upon the bound of Blanc et al. and holds under a strictly broader class of distributions. Moreover, we present an algorithm based on the top-down greedy heuristic that is entirely parameter-free -- it requires no prior knowledge of the optimal tree's size or depth -- offering a practical advantage over Blanc et al.'s method.
core_methodology: The paper rigorously analyzes the theoretical guarantees and performance bounds of the top-down greedy heuristic for training decision trees under arbitrary product distributions. It provides complexity bounds for approximating optimal decision trees, which is a foundational machine learning algorithm.
data_sources: The paper discusses theoretical bounds applicable to various input distributions, which, in a finance context, would refer to structured market feature sets (e.g., fundamental data, technical indicators, or alternative data features) designed to predict market outcomes.
alpha_potential: Decision trees (and related ensembles like Random Forests or Gradient Boosting) are staple algorithms in quantitative finance for classification (e.g., predicting direction) or regression (e.g., predicting returns). While the paper focuses on the theoretical guarantees of the basic greedy heuristic, understanding its behavior under non-uniform distributions is crucial for knowing when these models will generalize well on real, often skewed, financial time series data. The parameter-free aspect offers practical benefits for automated strategy development.
title_cn: 产品空间上的决策树学习
summary_cn: 该研究提供了决策树贪婪启发式算法在任意产品分布下的理论性能保证，扩展了现有均匀分布下的分析。这对于在具有复杂特征依赖性的真实金融数据上构建稳健、无需预设参数的决策模型（如分类或回归模型）具有实际意义，有助于提升策略的泛化能力和稳定性。

title: Universal Approximation of Nonlinear Operators and Their Derivatives
summary: Establishing Universal Approximation Theorems (UATs) for nonlinear operators and their derivatives is a foundational open problem in Operator Learning (OL) and raises delicate questions in Nonlinear Functional Analysis. We prove the first UATs for $k$-times differentiable nonlinear operators and their derivatives via OL architectures, uniformly on compact sets and in weighted Bastiani--Sobolev spaces for general finite input measures. In full Banach-space generality, these are the first complete generalizations of the corresponding influential classical UATs in [Hornik, 1991] to infinite-dimensional spaces and OL and they launch Derivative-Informed Operator Learning (DIOL)-learning nonlinear operators and their derivatives-on general Banach spaces. Based on our UATs, we formulate Bastiani--Sobolev training in DIOL. We present open frontiers where DIOL and our UATs find applications: high-order accuracy in OL; fast constrained optimization in Banach spaces (e.g. optimal control of PDEs, inverse problems) via Learn-Then-Optimize; numerical methods for infinite-dimensional PDEs (e.g. HJB PDEs on Banach spaces from infinite-dimensional optimal control via Optimize-Then-Learn, such as optimal control of PDEs, SPDEs, path-dependent systems, partially observed systems, mean-field control). We parameterize nonlinear operators via Encoder-Decoder Architectures, classical OL architectures. These include DeepONets, Deep-H-ONets, and PCA-Nets, which our UATs cover. Our UATs are based on (i) Approximation Properties of Banach spaces; (ii) continuous Bastiani differentiability (weaker than continuous Fr\'echet differentiability); (iii) $C^k_B$ (Bastiani) compact-open topologies; indeed, UA in $C^k$ (Fr\'echet) compact-open topologies (induced by operator norms) fails; (iv) construction of weighted Bastiani--Sobolev spaces, generalizing classical Gaussian Sobolev spaces on Banach spaces.
core_methodology: The paper establishes foundational Universal Approximation Theorems (UATs) proving that Operator Learning (OL) architectures, like DeepONets, can uniformly approximate $k$-times differentiable nonlinear operators and their derivatives on compact sets in general Banach spaces. It introduces Derivative-Informed Operator Learning (DIOL) methods for training these approximations.
data_sources: The theoretical framework applies to general functional spaces (e.g., Banach spaces) and operator mappings, which could represent complex, high-dimensional financial mappings, such as mapping market state vectors to optimal trading policies or volatility surfaces.
alpha_potential: While highly theoretical, the core contribution offers a stronger mathematical foundation for using deep learning models (specifically Operator Learning architectures) to approximate complex, non-linear functions representing system dynamics. In finance, this is highly relevant for modeling systems where the function to be learned is an *operator*—a mapping between function spaces—rather than a mapping between simple vectors. This is critical for areas like optimal control of stochastic processes (e.g., PDEs governing option pricing or portfolio constraints), and learning the evolution of complex systems (e.g., modeling mean-field dynamics). The ability to accurately approximate derivatives ($	ext{DIOL}$) is crucial for efficient optimization and constrained control in these high-dimensional settings, potentially leading to more robust and faster optimization techniques for large-scale portfolio optimization or path-dependent derivative pricing.
title_cn: 非线性算子及其导数的通用逼近
summary_cn: 该研究为算子学习（OL）架构逼近非线性算子及其导数提供了严格的数学基础。在金融领域，这意味着可以使用如DeepONet等模型，在巴拿赫空间这一更广的函数空间中，精确建模复杂的金融算子，例如路径依赖衍生品的定价或随机控制下的最优投资组合问题。理论成果支持了导数信息增强的算子学习（DIOL），可提升高阶精度求解无限维偏微分方程（如HJB方程），从而加速复杂金融模型的校准和优化。

title: MBABench: Evaluating LLM Agents on End-to-End Spreadsheet Tasks in Finance
summary: LLM agents are increasingly expected to carry out end-to-end workflows, producing complete artifacts from high-level user instructions. To meet enterprise needs, frontier AI labs have developed agents that can construct entire spreadsheets from scratch. This is especially relevant in finance, where core workflows such as financial modeling, forecasting, and scenario analysis are commonly conducted through spreadsheets. Yet, existing spreadsheet benchmarks do not measure this advanced capability, focusing instead on question-answering or single-formula edits. To address this gap, we provide one of the first evaluations of agents on end-to-end spreadsheet tasks, focusing on economically critical financial workflows such as modeling and scenario analysis. Since deliverables therein are routinely reviewed and revised by multiple stakeholders, judging their quality necessarily involves high-level criteria such as readability or ease of modification. To reflect the multidimensional nature of solution quality, we develop an evaluation taxonomy comprising three dimensions: Accuracy, Formula, and Format, each comprising fine-grained criteria that reflect professional standards. The Claude family leads the benchmark and produces the most professional-looking outputs in our qualitative review, but even the strongest agents frequently fall short of professional finance standards and degrade sharply as the difficulty increases beyond a few chained calculations. This suggests that current agents are not yet able to reliably produce professional-quality spreadsheets at the level of complexity real-world workflows demand.
core_methodology: Evaluation of Large Language Model (LLM) agents on constructing and executing complex, end-to-end spreadsheet tasks relevant to financial workflows (modeling, forecasting, scenario analysis). The study focuses on dimensional evaluation criteria: Accuracy, Formula correctness, and Format quality.
data_sources: Simulated financial workflows and tasks requiring spreadsheet construction and manipulation, reflecting real-world enterprise financial documents rather than live market data.
alpha_potential: Low direct alpha potential, as the paper evaluates LLM capabilities for automating analytical/modeling tasks rather than generating trading signals directly. However, high relevance for quantitative workflow automation. Agents that can reliably automate complex financial modeling tasks (risk assessment, scenario construction, automated report generation) reduce operational latency and analyst time, indirectly improving the speed and quality of quantitative strategy deployment and backtesting.
title_cn: MBABench：在金融领域评估LLM代理在端到端电子表格任务上的表现
summary_cn: 该研究评测了LLM代理完成复杂金融电子表格任务（如建模和情景分析）的能力。虽然当前代理在保持专业级准确性和复杂性方面仍有不足，但它们正逐渐应用于量化研究流程。成功实现电子表格自动化将显著提高量化团队构建模型、进行风险分析和测试策略的效率，为前沿策略的快速部署奠定基础。

title: Worse than Random: The Importance of a Baseline for Unsupervised Feature Selection
summary: Many novel unsupervised feature selection methods are proposed each year, yet their empirical evaluation is limited to supervised and unsupervised evaluation metrics computed on selected datasets, along with comparisons to existing methods. However, in the absence of an established evaluation baseline, it is difficult to determine the value added to the existing literature by each of these methods, and how effective their underlying approaches are. We propose using random feature selection as a baseline for evaluating the unsupervised feature selection methods. We empirically show that many of the state-of-the-art methods in unsupervised feature selection are outperformed by random feature selection in both performance and efficiency. Accordingly, we emphasize on the strict requirement of considering random feature selection as a baseline in the development process of novel unsupervised feature selection methods to ensure a consistent improvement over random feature selection.
core_methodology: This paper introduces a critical evaluation methodology for unsupervised feature selection (UFS) techniques, emphasizing the use of random feature selection as a required baseline. It argues that state-of-the-art UFS methods often fail to significantly outperform random selection under this strict benchmark.
data_sources: The paper focuses on general datasets used for algorithm evaluation, not specifically financial market data. However, the methodology is intended to be applied to any dataset, including high-dimensional financial feature sets.
alpha_potential: The relevance to alpha generation is indirect but crucial. In quantitative finance, many potential signals (features) are derived from unstructured or high-dimensional data (e.g., alternative data, news sentiment, technical indicators). If a sophisticated feature selection method consistently performs worse than random selection, deploying it in a trading strategy is detrimental. This paper provides a necessary sanity check: any proposed feature selection technique meant to reduce dimensionality or extract predictive features for trading models must first prove it significantly beats random selection efficiency and accuracy.
title_cn: 比随机更差：无监督特征选择的基准重要性
summary_cn: 该研究强调了在评估无监督特征选择（UFS）方法时，必须将随机特征选择作为基准。在量化交易中，从高维数据中筛选有效因子至关重要。此发现警示研究人员，许多复杂的特征选择算法可能不如随机选择有效。任何计划用于构建交易信号或因子模型的特征选择方法，都必须证明其优于随机基准，以确保对模型性能的实际贡献。

title: Neuronal Stochastic Attention Circuit (NSAC) for Probabilistic Representation Learning
summary: Reliable uncertainty quantification in continuous-time (CT) representation learning remains nascent, particularly within CT attention literature. We introduce the Neuronal Stochastic Attention Circuit (NSAC), a novel biologically-inspired CT attention architecture that reformulates attention logit computation as the solution of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck stochastic differential equation modulated by input-dependent, nonlinear interlinked gates derived from repurposed C. elegans Neuronal Circuit Policies (NCPs) wiring mechanism. It induces a Gaussian distribution over logits that propagates principled stochasticity through a logistic-normal distribution over attention weights to yield probabilistic output. A two-term objective function combining Gaussian negative log-likelihood with an epistemic-separation regularizer enforces higher predictive variance under distributional shifts and enables joint quantification of aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty. Theoretically, we provide: (i) state stability bounds; (ii) closed-form guarantees; and (iii) frozen-coefficient error approximation. Empirically, we implement NSAC in a diverse set of learning tasks including: (i) irregular CT function approximation; (ii) multivariate regression; (iii) long-range forecasting; (iv) Industry 4.0; and (v) lane-keeping of autonomous vehicles. We observe that NSAC remains competitive against several baselines in terms of accuracy and produces informative uncertainty estimates while being interpretable at the neuronal cell level.
core_methodology: The paper introduces the Neuronal Stochastic Attention Circuit (NSAC), a novel attention mechanism that uses a biologically-inspired architecture based on C. elegans Neuronal Circuit Policies (NCPs) to model attention logits as solutions to an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE). This results in a probabilistic (Gaussian) distribution over logits and a logistic-normal distribution over attention weights, providing principled uncertainty quantification. It also includes a regularization term to separate aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty.
data_sources: The empirical evaluation uses diverse tasks, including irregular continuous-time function approximation, multivariate regression, and long-range forecasting. For direct financial application, this methodology would need to be applied to time series data such as high-frequency market data, tick data, or fundamental indicators which exhibit complex temporal dependencies and stochasticity.
alpha_potential: The core value for quantitative finance lies in the NSAC's ability to produce robust, principled uncertainty quantification (UQ) within a continuous-time framework. In trading, uncertainty estimates (especially distinguishing aleatoric noise from epistemic model uncertainty) are crucial for risk management, position sizing, and dynamic portfolio allocation. A model that reliably estimates its own predictive variance under distributional shifts (model robustness) is valuable for adapting strategies to sudden market regime changes, enhancing trading signal reliability, and implementing more intelligent stop-loss/take-profit mechanisms.
title_cn: 用于概率表征学习的神经随机注意力电路（NSAC）
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种基于动态SDE和生物启发架构的新型注意力机制NSAC，旨在对连续时间表征学习中的不确定性进行可靠量化。其核心优势在于能区分偶然性（aleatoric）和认知性（epistemic）不确定性，这对于金融时间序列预测至关重要。在交易中，NSAC可用于实现更审慎的风险管理、自适应头寸规模调整以及在市场状态变化时进行可靠的预测和信号评估。

title: PJ-RoPE: A Fourier-Jet-Affine Position Space for Relative Attention
summary: We organize relative-position mechanisms in attention as a learnable Fourier-Jet-Affine position space. The starting point is lag-shift dynamics: a relative-position kernel is a response function of the lag \(d=i-j\), and the one-step shift \((Ef)(d)=f(d+1)\) gives a compact classification of finite structured responses through constant-coefficient difference modules. In this view, RoPE supplies simple Fourier roots, Jordan-RoPE thickens these roots into finite Fourier jets, and ALiBi supplies the repeated unit-root affine direction. NTK-aware RoPE scaling fits the same structure as a spectral flow of simple Fourier roots: moving the frequency grid generates first Fourier-jet tangent directions, while higher Taylor directions generate higher jets. PJ-RoPE makes these jet directions explicit and learnable, and uses the resulting space to measure task-level sector selection. The framework separates scalar PJ-bias kernels from exact PJ-rotary feature transforms, introduces sector-gate, effective-mass, functional-energy, and leave-one-order-out diagnostics, and stabilizes high-order coordinates with LC/rapidity compactification. Controlled probes recover designed sectors; synthetic teachers show trainable use; small byte-level language runs favor NTK-aware RoPE plus affine recency; symbolic music-token streams keep LC/affine variants strong with measurable high-order corrections; and LC diagnostics quantify the stability-resolution tradeoff.
core_methodology: PJ-RoPE introduces a learnable Fourier-Jet-Affine position space to formalize relative attention mechanisms, building upon existing techniques like RoPE and ALiBi. It refines attention by explicitly modeling higher-order relative position interactions using Fourier jets and introduces novel components like sector-gate and effective-mass kernels for structured representation and analysis. The framework is demonstrated primarily in language and symbolic sequence modeling tasks.
data_sources: Primarily uses language and symbolic music token streams for model training and diagnostics. While not directly financial data, the methodology is applicable to any sequential data, including time series.
alpha_potential: The potential benefit lies in improving the modeling of temporal dependencies in sequential data, which is crucial for time-series forecasting in finance. Specifically, the ability to explicitly model and control higher-order relative positional information (via Fourier jets) could enhance long-range dependency capture in financial time series prediction, potentially improving momentum, regime detection, or microstructure modeling, especially where complex lag structures exist. However, practical implementation in trading requires adapting the 'sector selection' concept to financial groupings or features.
title_cn: PJ-RoPE：用于相对注意力的傅里叶射流仿射位置空间
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种新的相对注意力机制框架PJ-RoPE，利用可学习的傅里叶-射流-仿射空间来精确捕捉时间序列中的相对位置信息。该方法提升了处理长期依赖的能力，对于金融时间序列预测（如高频数据或长期因子建模）具有理论借鉴价值，可作为改进Transformer模型结构以增强金融信号捕获的潜在工具。

title: DN-Hypo-Pipeline: An AI-Driven Workflow for Generating Hypotheses using Large Language Models and Scientific Explanations
summary: A scientific hypothesis is the first step in research and undergoes experimental validation, yet it also reflects a deep understanding of and reasoning about scientific phenomena. We introduce DN-Hypo-Pipeline, an AI-powered workflow based on large language models, designed to support structured scientific thinking and hypothesis generation by leveraging scientific explanations as prior knowledge. This pipeline assists researchers in deriving novel hypotheses from existing literature. Given the explanandum (i.e., the conclusion) of a research paper, it identifies underlying laws, theories, and principles, and reconstructs a new, yet-to-be-verified explanation for the observed phenomenon. We evaluated DN-Hypo-Pipeline in the field of data science modeling using three highly cited papers. Statistical inference, supported by both LLM-as-judge assessment and human expert evaluation, demonstrates that our pipeline is more effective than direct generation methods. Additionally, we validated the two highest-scoring generated hypotheses by developing corresponding novel algorithms, which outperformed the baseline models presented in the original papers. Beyond application in data science, DN-Hypo-Pipeline provides a theoretical framework that not only encompasses theory-guided data science modeling methods but also reveals a more fundamental structure of the modeling process. Moreover, this approach is essentially a generalization of theory-guided modeling, offering potential for extension to other domains and across a broader range of scientific disciplines.
core_methodology: The core methodology is an AI-driven workflow (DN-Hypo-Pipeline) utilizing Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate structured scientific hypotheses. It uses existing scientific explanations (literature) as prior knowledge to derive novel, verifiable explanations for observed phenomena (explanandum). The key mechanism is reasoning from known principles to infer unverified conclusions, aiming for structured, theory-guided discovery.
data_sources: The paper primarily uses scientific literature and data science modeling papers as input for hypothesis generation. However, the framework itself is domain-agnostic. Practically, the data sources for quantitative finance would involve academic finance literature, regulatory filings, market data, and empirical results that serve as the 'explanandum' for hypothesis generation.
alpha_potential: The paper demonstrates that hypotheses generated via this structured reasoning process can lead to the development of novel algorithms that outperform existing baselines. In finance, this pipeline could be used to: 1) Systematically generate novel factor hypotheses by synthesizing complex relationships found in financial theory and empirical studies. 2) Discover non-obvious regime transitions or market dynamics that current models overlook by forcing the LLM to explain anomalies (explananda) using established financial principles. While the direct output is a hypothesis, the validated success of generated algorithms suggests a clear path to developing new alpha signals.
title_cn: DN-Hypo-Pipeline：一种利用大型语言模型和科学解释生成研究假设的人工智能驱动工作流
summary_cn: DN-Hypo-Pipeline 框架利用 LLM 和既有科学解释，系统性地从现有金融文献中推导出新颖、可验证的量化交易假设。该方法可用于加速因子发现和模型创新，通过结构化推理生成超越现有基准的新颖算法。

title: Bellman-sufficient Information Complexity
summary: We develop Bellman-sufficient information complexity, a representation-level framework for studying information-theoretic complexity in sequential decision making. The primitive object is an environment space $\Omega$ and an admissible algorithm class. The intrinsic object is a Bellman-sufficient state representation together with an information index $Y=\chi(\Omega)$, often the optimal decision or value object rather than the full environment. This replaces syntactic model realizability with representation-level sufficiency for decision making. On the upper-bound side, learning is organized as a dynamic program on the sufficient state with a logarithmic information potential for the index. In fixed-truth analysis this potential is represented by the coordinate log loss $\gamma\log(1/q_t(\chi(\omega^\star)))$; in the indexed Algorithmic Information Ratio (AIR) regret identities it gives rise to the log-posterior telescope, and after Bayesian posterior averaging it corresponds to an entropy term. On the lower side, a Bellman-Fano certificate uses the same state and index to compare the indexed information telescope with the ghost-good mass of low-regret reference trajectories. The central matching statement is therefore a conditional Bellman information-risk sandwich when the log-penalized Bellman upper value and the ghost-quantile lower certificate close on the same representation and at the same radius. UCB, E2D/DEC, and AMS/EBO then appear as tractable certificates or relaxations of this same log-potential Bellman program, rather than as separate notions of information complexity.
core_methodology: The paper introduces 'Bellman-sufficient information complexity,' a framework for sequential decision-making. It centers on identifying 'sufficient state representations' (the 'index' $Y$) that encapsulate the necessary information for optimal decision-making (like a value function or optimal action) by replacing the full environment description with a compact, information-efficient representation. It uses concepts like information potential (log loss, entropy term) and Bellman equations to bound learning performance, unifying concepts like UCB, E2D/DEC, and AMS/EBO under this framework.
data_sources: The framework is general to sequential decision environments. For trading, this implies data used for state representation in Reinforcement Learning (RL) or sequential modeling, such as price histories, order book data, or time-series features.
alpha_potential: While highly theoretical, this framework provides a rigorous foundation for understanding the complexity limits of state representation in reinforcement learning applied to sequential financial tasks (like optimal trade execution or dynamic portfolio sizing). By formalizing what information is truly 'sufficient' for decision-making, it could lead to more sample-efficient and robust RL agents, potentially speeding up convergence in complex market environments where data is scarce or high-frequency.
title_cn: 贝尔曼充分信息复杂度
summary_cn: 该研究提出一种用于序贯决策的理论框架，旨在确定做出最优决策所需的最小充分信息集（状态表示）。对量化交易而言，这为构建更高效、收敛更快的强化学习（RL）模型提供了理论基础，尤其在需要从复杂数据中提取关键决策信息的场景，如最优执行或动态风险管理。

title: A Riemannian Approach to Low-Rank Optimal Transport
summary: Low-rank optimal transport (OT) mitigates the quadratic scaling of classical solvers, yet existing approaches rely heavily on first-order mirror-descent updates that require careful hyperparameter tuning and ignore the optimization landscape's curvature. To address these limitations, we propose a unified Riemannian geometric framework for low-rank OT, modeling balanced and unbalanced rank-$r$ positive factored couplings as novel smooth embedded submanifolds of the positive orthant. By equipping these manifolds with the Fisher-Rao product metric, we derive tractable formulations for Riemannian projectors, retractions, and Hessian-vector products. Our cost-agnostic framework seamlessly extends to linear OT, Gromov-Wasserstein (GW), fused GW, and their unbalanced counterparts. For balanced OT, our geometric ingredients are computed via efficient conjugate-gradient and iterative Bregman updates. For the unbalanced OT, our operations elegantly reduce to closed-form scalings, completely eliminating inner iterative loops. In both regimes, per-iteration complexity scales linearly with dataset size, and we provide a rank-sufficiency certificate for global optimality verification. Extensive experiments across a range of problem sizes demonstrate that our regularization-free first- and second-order solvers achieve faster convergence and superior performance over existing state-of-the-art low-rank OT solvers.
core_methodology: The paper develops a novel Riemannian geometric framework to solve low-rank Optimal Transport (OT) problems. It models factored couplings as submanifolds equipped with the Fisher-Rao metric, allowing for efficient, curvature-aware first- and second-order optimization algorithms that scale linearly with data size. This approach provides superior convergence speed compared to existing first-order methods for standard and unbalanced OT, Gromov-Wasserstein, and related problems.
data_sources: The methodology is general and data-agnostic, applicable to comparing distributions derived from any market data, such as historical time series, factor exposures, or high-frequency order book snapshots.
alpha_potential: Optimal Transport (OT) metrics, particularly Wasserstein distance, are powerful tools for comparing probability distributions (e.g., asset return distributions, volatility structures, or market state classifications). Applying this new, highly efficient low-rank Riemannian solver accelerates distribution comparison, which is crucial for applications like dynamic portfolio optimization (comparing current vs. target risk profiles), robust risk management (assessing distribution shifts), or advanced factor rotation/selection where comparing factor return distributions is key. The regularization-free, highly efficient solvers make complex OT-based comparisons feasible in high-frequency or large-scale environments.
title_cn: 低秩最优传输的黎曼几何方法
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种基于黎曼几何的高效低秩最优传输（OT）求解框架。它显著提升了比较金融数据分布（如资产回报率、风险暴露）的计算效率和收敛速度。该方法可应用于动态投资组合优化和风险管理，通过快速、正则化无关地比较不同市场状态或策略的分布，为因子选择和鲁棒性分析提供更优工具。

title: PolicyGuard: Towards Test-time and Step-level Adversary (Backdoor) Defense for Reinforcement Learning Agent
summary: While real-world applications of reinforcement learning (RL) are becoming increasingly popular, the security of RL systems deserve more attention and exploration. In particular, recent work has revealed that RL agents are vulnerable to backdoor attacks, where a victim agent behaves normally under standard conditions but executes malicious actions when a specific trigger is activated. Existing backdoor defenses for RL either require access to the agent's internal parameters, operate only at the model or trajectory level, or are limited to specific attack types. To ensure the security of RL agents, we propose \texttt{PolicyGuard}, a \textit{test-time step-level} backdoor defense which leverages Gaussian Process (GP) posterior variance and adapts pseudo trajectories to enable uncertainty computation for individual time step. Besides, we also provide theoretical foundations to explain the efficacy of GP posterior variance. Extensive experiments across seven RL games demonstrate that PolicyGuard achieves state-of-the-art detection performance in most cases, with average AUROC of 0.856 for perturbation-based attacks and 0.859 for adversary-agent attacks.
core_methodology: PolicyGuard introduces a test-time, step-level backdoor defense for Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents. It leverages Gaussian Process (GP) posterior variance to compute uncertainty regarding individual time steps, using adapted pseudo trajectories to detect malicious triggers activated by specific patterns (backdoors) in the input environment. This method aims to ensure the security and robustness of deployed RL models.
data_sources: The primary data source mentioned are 'RL games' used for extensive testing (seven environments). In a financial context, this methodology would be applied to time-series data, market order flow, or simulated trading environments where the RL agent interacts.
alpha_potential: While the paper is focused on general RL security rather than generating alpha, its practical value stems from **risk management and strategy robustness**. In quantitative finance, RL agents are used for execution, portfolio management, and high-frequency trading. Adversarial attacks (backdoors) could lead to catastrophic losses if an attacker exploits a hidden trigger to force the agent into undesirable trades. PolicyGuard offers a mechanism to make deployed RL trading algorithms more resilient and trustworthy by detecting malicious inputs or state perturbations in real-time, thereby protecting existing alpha-generating strategies.
title_cn: PolicyGuard：面向测试时间和步进级别的强化学习代理的后门防御
summary_cn: 该研究提出PolicyGuard，一种用于强化学习（RL）交易代理的测试时步进级后门防御机制。它利用高斯过程（GP）的后验方差来检测特定触发器激活时的恶意行为。这对于保护部署在真实交易环境中的RL算法至关重要，可有效防止因外部恶意输入导致策略执行灾难性错误，增强模型的鲁棒性和安全性。

title: Circuit Synchronization Precedes Generalization: A Causal Precursor to Grokking
summary: Grokking is the delayed generalisation phenomenon where a transformer trained on modular arithmetic abruptly transitions from near-chance to near-perfect validation accuracy. It has been attributed to a Fourier-based algorithmic circuit, but its timing, causal structure, and controllability remain poorly understood. We introduce the Frequency Synchronization Degree (FSD), a normalised, permutation-tested metric for Fourier circuit synchronisation requiring no prior knowledge of the circuit. Across nine modular addition configurations (five primes, three seeds), FSD reaches its post-grokking level 500 to 3000 steps before grokking (mean lead 1722 steps, every configuration positive, sign-test p approx 0.004), and synchronises before a restricted-logit loss baseline in all nine cases, making it the earliest available predictor. We give direct causal evidence that the inter-phase gap is a regularisation phenomenon: forking training at the FSD-ceiling step and varying weight decay lambda produces monotonically earlier grokking, with delta-t proportional to 1/lambda. This law replicates across three primes (R-squared 0.89 to 0.99 on seed-averaged delta-t); per-run R-squared is unstable due to the chaotic transition, so we report error bars rather than single runs. Grokking occurs at a near-constant memorisation norm across lambda, grounding the constant in a threshold mechanism. This is not an artefact of applying a Fourier detector to a Fourier circuit: on the non-abelian group S5, a basis-faithful generalisation of FSD precedes grokking on all six seeds, while the original Fourier FSD does not. Using the FSD ceiling to schedule a weight-decay increase also accelerates grokking over a fixed schedule without destabilising training. An attention-only variant groks with a strong FSD precursor while an MLP-only model never groks.
core_methodology: The core methodology introduces the Frequency Synchronization Degree (FSD) as a novel, early-warning metric for predicting the 'grokking' phenomenon in transformer models—specifically, the delayed generalization observed in modular arithmetic tasks. It establishes a causal relationship between FSD synchronization and the onset of generalization, demonstrating that FSD acts as an earliest predictor (leading grokking by thousands of steps) and that training schedules (via weight decay) can be optimized based on FSD thresholds to accelerate generalization.
data_sources: The primary data source is synthetic datasets based on modular arithmetic (e.g., modular addition over prime groups like Zp), used to train and analyze transformer models, rather than real-world financial market data.
alpha_potential: While this paper does not present a direct trading signal, its findings are highly relevant to the application of sophisticated machine learning models (like Transformers) in quantitative finance. The ability to reliably predict when a model transitions from memorization (overfitting) to true generalization (robustness) is crucial. In trading, this translates directly to knowing when a complex Q-model trained on market dynamics will likely start providing reliable out-of-sample signals versus when it is merely overfitting noise. Identifying early precursors like FSD could enable superior model deployment scheduling or dynamic risk management based on the internal state of the trading AI.
title_cn: 电路同步先于泛化：Grokking 的一个因果前兆
summary_cn: 该研究提出了频率同步度（FSD）作为衡量Transformer模型内部电路同步性的新指标，能比传统方法提前数千步预测模型延迟泛化（Grokking）的发生。对于量化交易而言，这意味着可以提前识别复杂AI模型（如用于预测或执行的Transformer）何时从过拟合训练数据转变为产生真正稳健的、可泛化的预测。此发现有助于优化AI模型的部署时机和调优训练策略，从而提高策略的鲁棒性和实盘表现。

title: Certified World Models: Predictability Across Configuration, Horizon, and Resolution
summary: Scale buys interpolation; structure buys certifiable transfer. A world model's average error does not say whether a particular rollout can be trusted, or for how long. For equivariant latent world models we give a predictability certificate: a computable region spanning configuration, horizon, and resolution. Under exact equivariance, rollout error is invariant over the monoid generated by k primitive symmetries and is certified from the k generators (Theorem A); universal orbit-flatness over equivariant targets characterizes equivariance at the function level (Lemma 2), so an unconstrained architecture cannot certify the property by construction. Approximate orbit-transfer defects propagate by the finite-time Lyapunov spectrum (Theorem B): expanding channels give a logarithmic horizon $T_j(\epsilon)\sim\log(1/\epsilon)/\lambda_j$, neutral channels accumulate recurrent defect linearly, and contracting channels accumulate a bounded nonzero floor. Exact conserved charge values are certified to all horizons only at zero defect; with one-step defect $\eta$, charge-value error grows at most as $T\eta$. Empirically, on a 40-dimensional learned model a $\mathbb{Z}_N$-equivariant network recovers the full Lyapunov spectrum ($R^2=0.98$-$0.99$) where dense and recurrent baselines fail. A cone/adapted-metric certificate reads an a-priori horizon off the model's own Jacobian, tight on uniformly hyperbolic dynamics and self-abstaining elsewhere; the resulting horizon improves a budgeted re-observation decision. For public non-equivariant world models the tangent spectrum gives a training-free candidate horizon, paired with a held-out divergence cross-check that abstains or corrects when the learned loop over-promises.
core_methodology: The core methodology involves developing 'predictability certificates' for equivariant latent world models. This uses concepts from dynamical systems, specifically Lyapunov exponents and tangent spectrum analysis, to quantify the uncertainty and prediction horizon of a model's rollout based on its underlying symmetries (e.g., $\mathbb{Z}_N$-equivariance) and structural properties (e.g., orbit-flatness). It provides a non-parametric way to estimate reliability based on the model's internal geometry.
data_sources: The abstract discusses general 'world models' and uses empirical examples on a 40-dimensional learned model. While not explicitly mentioning financial data, the framework is designed to be applied to sequential, dynamic systems, implying time-series data typical in finance (e.g., price paths, order book dynamics, macroeconomic indicators) used to train such world models.
alpha_potential: The practical value lies in robustly estimating the trustworthy prediction horizon ($T$) for sequential predictions made by complex AI models (like those based on Transformers or complex latent dynamics models trained on market data). In algorithmic trading, knowing *when* a forecast becomes unreliable (i.e., when the error budget exceeds the required threshold for a given strategy execution) is critical. This allows a system to switch from predictive control to reactive/model-free control, or to correctly size exposure based on forecast reliability, which is particularly useful for high-frequency or medium-frequency momentum/mean-reversion signals derived from learned world dynamics.
title_cn: 可验证的世界模型：跨配置、时间跨度和分辨率的可预测性
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种针对等变世界模型的预测性证书，用来量化模型预测的可靠时间范围。这对于构建基于复杂动力学学习的交易策略至关重要。通过计算模型的李雅普诺夫谱和切线谱，可以直接估计预测的有效信息窗口（预测视野），帮助算法交易系统根据预测的可信度动态调整交易决策和风险敞口。

title: Simplex-Constrained Sparse Bagging: Transitioning from Uniform Priors to Sparse Posteriors in Ensemble Learning
summary: We present Simplex-Constrained Sparse Bagging (SCSB), a mathematically rigorous framework for post-training compression and probability calibration of bootstrap-based bagging ensembles. Standard bagging ensembles (such as Random Forests, Bagged SVMs, and Bagged Neural Networks) assign uniform voting power to all constituent estimators. However, this naive uniform prior ignores the varying local competence of base estimators and contributes to model overconfidence. We formulate ensemble pruning and calibration as a joint optimization problem over the probability simplex by minimizing the Out-Of-Bag (OOB) loss. To induce sparsity, we address the theoretical "L1-simplex paradox" - the mathematical reality that the L1 norm is constant on the simplex and fails to prune - by introducing a concave quadratic penalty. SCSB is model-agnostic and achieves up to 96% ensemble compression, yielding linear inference speedups and superior probability calibration (lowered Expected Calibration Error) while preserving or enhancing generalization accuracy.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Simplex-Constrained Sparse Bagging (SCSB), a method to refine traditional bagging ensembles (like Random Forests) by moving from uniform weighting to sparse weighting of base estimators. It uses a joint optimization framework minimizing Out-Of-Bag (OOB) loss subject to simplex constraints, incorporating a concave quadratic penalty for sparsity. This achieves model compression, faster inference, and better probability calibration.
data_sources: The methodology is generally model-agnostic, meaning it can be applied to any model trained using bootstrap aggregation. In the context of trading, this would typically involve time-series financial data (e.g., price/volume data for signal generation) or alternative datasets used to train constituent classifiers/regressors.
alpha_potential: While not a direct trading strategy, SCSB addresses a crucial aspect of deploying complex ML models in trading: model robustness, inference speed, and, critically, accurate probability calibration. In finance, overconfident predictions (poor calibration) lead to significant estimation risk. By improving calibration (lowering ECE) and increasing inference speed (up to 96% compression), SCSB makes complex ensemble models more reliable and deployable in latency-sensitive quantitative trading systems.
title_cn: 单形约束稀疏Bagging：从集成学习中的均匀先验到稀疏后验的转变
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种名为SCSB的框架，用于压缩和校准Bagging集成模型。在量化交易中，通过引入稀疏加权来替代传统的均匀投票，SCSB能显著提升模型推理速度（高达96%压缩）。最重要的是，它改善了模型的概率校准，降低了过度自信预测的风险，这对于构建稳健、可靠的金融风险预测和分类模型至关重要。

title: GitOfThoughts: Version-Controlled Reasoning and Agent Memory You Can Replay, Diff, and Merge
summary: Large language model reasoning leaves no trace once it is done. The steps of a chain of thought disappear when the context window closes, a pruned search branch is just gone, and memory buffers cannot be diffed, merged, or audited. Code, infrastructure, and experiments are all version-controlled. Reasoning is not. GitOfThoughts stores an agent's reasoning tree as a git repository. Every scored thought becomes a commit, scores become notes, outcomes become tags, and retrieval is just git log over the agent's own history. We use this to test something simple. Does giving an agent memory from past problems actually make it more accurate? We tried five memory stores (none, a markdown file, a vector database, a graph, and git) across two benchmarks, two model sizes, and several pre-registered repeat experiments. The answer, on new problems, is no, including one promising early result that did not hold up when we repeated it. Memory only helps once the problem being solved is nearly identical to something already in memory (cosine similarity above about 0.8); below that, it does nothing. In other words, the model is finding the answer rather than learning the method. Even a model 4.5x larger still cannot pull a reusable method out of a worked example; it just gets better at spotting near-copies. The only thing that reliably helped on new problems was generating several answers and picking the most common one (self-consistency). So the case for using git as the memory store is not that it retrieves better. It is that it gives auditability, history, and the ability to merge two agents' memories, at no cost to accuracy.
core_methodology: The core methodology involves tracking and version-controlling the entire reasoning process of an AI agent using a Git repository structure. Each step (thought) is a commit, and outcomes are tagged. This creates an auditable, replayable, and mergeable history of agent decisions, contrasting with standard context-window-based reasoning.
data_sources: The evaluation uses general language model benchmarks and problems, not specific financial market data. The primary 'data' explored here is the agent's own internal reasoning/memory states.
alpha_potential: While the paper does not yield direct alpha, it addresses a critical pain point in advanced AI trading: debugging, auditing, and improving complex, multi-step trading logic generated by LLM agents. The ability to 'diff' and 'merge' different agents' reasoning histories could allow quants to systematically combine successful decision paths from separate development streams, a key component for building robust, explainable trading systems based on LLMs. However, the paper's finding that memory only helps for near-identical problems suggests caution regarding using past trades directly as memory for generating new strategies.
title_cn: GitOfThoughts：可回放、可差异化比较和可合并的受版本控制的推理与智能体记忆
summary_cn: 该研究提出使用Git来版本控制大型语言模型（LLM）的推理过程，使其具备可审计性、可回放性。尽管在通用问题上，外部记忆对提高新问题准确性帮助不大，该技术为量化交易中基于LLM智能体的复杂决策提供了必要的追踪、调试和合并机制，从而增强了模型可解释性和策略迭代效率。

title: PrologMCP: A Standardized Prolog Tool Interface for LLM Agents
summary: Frontier reasoning-tuned language models still fail on deductive tasks at depth, and the cost of improved performance through extended internal reasoning scales poorly. Symbolic delegation offers a complementary route: a language model translates the problem, while a solver performs the inference. However, current autoformalization pipelines for logic programming are typically bespoke integrations tied to particular tasks or agents. We introduce PrologMCP, a task-agnostic, open-source server that exposes Prolog as a stateful tool through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Its compact tool interface, structured error reporting, and per-session isolation make the translate-run-inspect-repair loop a reusable primitive for MCP-capable agents. We evaluate a formalizer agent enhanced with PrologMCP against standard and reasoning LLMs (Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-4.1, and o4-mini) on two subsets of PARARULE-Plus: a general-purpose sample and a more challenging one targeting a specific failure mode of natural-language reasoning. On the general sample, the formalizer matches or exceeds reasoning LLMs (accuracy 1.00 vs.\ 1.00 / 0.998), with the largest gains over standard models (0.762 for GPT-4.1). On the challenging subset, the formalizer remains near-perfect (1.00 / 0.99) while reasoning LLMs drop to 0.95 / 0.94. These results suggest that delegating inference to Prolog via MCP is a robust and inspectable alternative to extended natural-language reasoning.
core_methodology: The paper introduces PrologMCP, a standardized interface (based on the Model Context Protocol - MCP) that allows Language Model (LLM) agents to delegate complex deductive and logical reasoning tasks to an external Prolog solver. This establishes a robust 'translate-run-inspect-repair' loop where the LLM formats problems into first-order logic queries for Prolog, and the solver executes the inference, providing structured, inspectable results back to the agent.
data_sources: The primary focus is on the methodology for improving LLM reasoning, evaluated on symbolic reasoning benchmarks (PARARULE-Plus). No direct financial data sources are utilized or discussed in the abstract.
alpha_potential: The direct alpha potential is low, as the paper focuses on foundational AI architecture rather than financial signals. However, the underlying capability—creating highly reliable, transparent, and auditable reasoning agents via LLM-Symbolic delegation—has significant potential. This architecture could be used to: 1) Formalize complex regulatory constraints or complex options/derivatives payoff structures into verifiable logic modules. 2) Improve due diligence and compliance checking where formal logic inference is required over unstructured data interpreted by the LLM. 3) Create agents capable of performing multi-step, verifiable trade execution logic.
title_cn: PrologMCP：一种用于LLM智能体的标准化Prolog工具接口
summary_cn: 该研究提出PrologMCP，一个允许大型语言模型（LLM）智能体将复杂的逻辑推理任务委托给Prolog求解器的标准化接口。此架构将LLM的自然语言理解与Prolog的精确符号推理相结合，显著提高了深度演绎任务的可靠性和可解释性。在量化交易中，此技术可用于构建更稳健、可验证的交易决策引擎，尤其是在处理复杂规则、合规性检查或需要严格逻辑链条的投资组合约束管理方面。

title: When Confidence Lacks Concepts: Interpretable OOD Detection via Representation Perturbations
summary: Deep neural networks have achieved remarkable performance across medical imaging tasks, yet their tendency to overgeneralize under distributional shifts poses a major obstacle to safe clinical deployment. Out-of-Distribution (OOD) detection methods aim to mitigate this risk, but most existing approaches rely on opaque internal signals with poorly understood semantic meaning, limiting trust in safety-critical settings. In this work, we propose an interpretable OOD detection framework that probes the stability of model predictions under class-conditioned semantic perturbations. Leveraging sparse autoencoders (SAEs), we learn class-specific concept vectors from in-distribution data that disentangle dense intermediate representations into sparse, semantically meaningful components. At inference, we perturb deeper-layer representations using the concept vectors associated with the model's predicted class and measure the class logits stability. We hypothesize that in-distribution samples exhibit low sensitivity to such perturbations, as their representations align with class-specific semantic directions, whereas OOD samples show amplified deviations due to representational misalignment. By framing OOD detection as a concept conditioned stability analysis, our approach provides both a discriminative OOD signal and an interpretable lens into the internal mechanisms driving model uncertainty, making it particularly suitable for high stakes medical applications.
core_methodology: The core methodology involves using Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to learn class-specific concept vectors from in-distribution data representations. These vectors are then used to perturb deeper-layer representations, and the stability of prediction logits under this class-conditioned semantic perturbation is measured to detect Out-of-Distribution (OOD) samples.
data_sources: The primary focus is on deep neural network representations learned from existing data, initially medical imaging in the abstract, but adaptable to financial time series or alternative data embeddings.
alpha_potential: While the paper focuses on safety-critical applications like medical imaging, the fundamental concept of measuring model stability against semantic perturbations provides a robust mechanism for detecting shifts in underlying data distributions (OOD). In finance, this translates directly to monitoring model risk. A significant application is identifying when market regimes have fundamentally shifted beyond the training distribution (e.g., a structural break, novel black swan event, or data corruption), which invalidates the current model's predictions. This is not a direct alpha signal but a critical risk management tool for high-frequency or complex ML-based strategies.
title_cn: 当信心缺乏概念时：通过表示扰动进行可解释的OOD检测
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种利用稀疏自编码器学习概念向量，并通过有条件的语义扰动来检测模型对新分布数据的敏感性。在量化交易中，该方法可用于评估机器学习模型在市场结构发生根本性变化（如概念漂移或市场剧变）时的鲁棒性，从而提供重要的风险管理信号，避免在模型失效的高风险时期进行交易或过度交易。

title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Reservoir Computing
summary: Reservoir computing offers a lightweight framework for forecasting dynamical systems but may struggle to capture long-range dependencies due to limited representational capacity. Conventional reservoir computing recurrently uses trainable reservoirs with hyperparameter sensitivity, while the next-generation reservoir computing removes recurrence at the cost of rapidly growing feature dimensions. Here, we develop Kolmogorov-Arnold Reservoir Computing (KARC), which replaces reservoirs with explicit basis-function expansions inspired by the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem. We rigorously show that KARC is a lightweight design of Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KANs), preserving the potential expressive capacity of KANs while admitting efficient closed-form training of reservoir computing. At comparable cost, KARC outperforms existing reservoir computing methods on challenging benchmarks including partial differential equations. It can also be integrated with generative diffusion models for text-to-image generation. This work thus establishes a principled bridge between reservoir computing and KANs, enabling efficient and high-fidelity dynamical system forecasting.
core_methodology: Kolmogorov-Arnold Reservoir Computing (KARC) replaces standard recurrent reservoirs with basis-function expansions inspired by the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem. This allows for efficient, closed-form training while theoretically preserving the high expressive capacity associated with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs). It is presented as a fixed-weight, lightweight forecasting framework.
data_sources: The paper uses dynamical system benchmarks, including partial differential equations, for validation. In a trading context, this framework would be applied to time-series data such as high-frequency market data, price series, or engineered features representing market states.
alpha_potential: KARC offers a potentially superior, computationally efficient alternative to standard Reservoir Computing (RC) for modeling complex, non-linear time-series dependencies. Since forecasting dynamical systems is the core problem in time series prediction (including price movements), KARC could be used to build high-fidelity, low-latency models for short-to-medium term prediction, especially in microstructure or high-frequency trading where the speed and stability of training (closed-form) are crucial. Its ability to capture long-range dependencies better than standard RC enhances its applicability for modeling longer-term market regimes or factors.
title_cn: Kolmogorov-Arnold 储层计算
summary_cn: KARC是一种基于Kolmogorov-Arnold定理的新型轻量级动力系统预测框架。它通过基函数展开替代传统循环结构，实现了高效的闭式训练，优化了对长期依赖性的捕获能力。该方法在时间序列预测方面具有潜力，可用于构建高保真、低延迟的市场短期预测模型，尤其适用于高频和微观结构交易策略的研发。

title: CRAX: Fast Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmarking
summary: Safety is a core concern for deploying reinforcement learning (RL) agents in real-world domains such as robotics and autonomous driving. While benchmarks have been central to progress in RL, existing safety benchmarks with high-fidelity 3D physics remain computationally slow, limiting large-scale experimentation and rapid prototyping. To address this gap, we propose CRAX (Constrained RL Accelerated with JAX). Built on top of the MuJoCo XLA (MJX) physics engine with realistic 3D dynamics, CRAX leverages vectorized operations and hardware acceleration, yielding up to ~100x speedups over comparable CPU-based safety benchmarks. The benchmark features six environment suites and three agent-specific tasks, each spanning three difficulty levels. Evaluating six popular safe RL methods shows that no single approach dominates across all tasks, and reveals the trade-offs between performance and safety. We find that curriculum learning across difficulty levels and safety transfer can improve performance over direct training in harder settings.
core_methodology: The core methodology involves accelerating Reinforcement Learning (RL) benchmarking, specifically Safe RL, by leveraging JAX and vectorized operations for significant speedups (~100x) in high-fidelity 3D physics environments (MuJoCo XLA). This allows for faster experimentation with constrained RL agents. Key findings relate to the trade-offs between performance and safety, and the benefit of curriculum learning and safety transfer.
data_sources: The benchmark uses simulated physics environments (robotics/autonomous driving settings) rather than real financial market data. However, the *methodological* output is applicable to training agents on market interaction data.
alpha_potential: While CRAX itself is not a trading strategy, the advancements in computationally efficient and safe RL benchmarking are highly valuable. Safe RL is critical for deploying agents in high-stakes financial environments like high-frequency trading or large portfolio management where constraint violations (e.g., excessive drawdowns, violating regulatory limits) are unacceptable. The speedups enable quicker iteration and better tuning of risk-aware RL algorithms needed for portfolio optimization and execution strategies.
title_cn: CRAX：快速安全强化学习基准测试
summary_cn: CRAX通过JAX加速了高保真3D物理环境中的安全强化学习（Safe RL）基准测试，实现了高达100倍的速度提升。这项技术进步对于开发受风险约束的金融交易代理至关重要，尤其是在投资组合优化和资产执行策略中，能显著加速高风险、高回报RL算法的迭代和安全验证。

title: Brownian Motion with a Pulse: A Biostatistician's Guide to Diffusions, Bridges, Functional PCA, and First-Passage Models
summary: Brownian motion is a compact mathematical language for continuous-time uncertainty in biostatistics. This tutorial develops the process from construction and path properties to tools that recur in applied biomedical work: the Markov and strong Markov properties, the Karhunen-Loeve expansion, functional principal component analysis (Functional PCA), reflection principles, local time, stochastic differential equations (SDEs), Brownian bridges, and empirical-process limits. The applications emphasize longitudinal biomarkers, degradation modelling, first-passage endpoints, dynamic frailty, group-sequential monitoring, calibration diagnostics, recurrent-event processes, electronic health records, and wearable streams. A short cross-domain section uses literary and historical archives to make Brownian-bridge thinking concrete without shifting the paper away from biostatistics, and includes a reproducible chapter-level experiment on Frankenstein. The Black-Merton-Scholes model is included as a solved SDE template, not as a finance application in its own right. The aim is to connect rigorous probability with modelling decisions faced by biostatisticians when biological processes evolve between noisy observation times.
core_methodology: The paper focuses on advanced stochastic modeling techniques, particularly Brownian motion extensions, SDEs, Functional PCA, and first-passage time models, presented through a biostatistics lens. While the core math is relevant, the primary application context is biomedical, not finance.
data_sources: The paper emphasizes longitudinal biomarkers, electronic health records, and wearable data streams. It explicitly mentions the Black-Merton-Scholes model as a solved SDE template, suggesting the mathematical tools are transferable to financial time series.
alpha_potential: The direct alpha potential is low as the applications are biomedical. However, the techniques—especially Functional PCA applied to continuous-time paths, Brownian bridges for interpolation/extrapolation between sparse observations, and first-passage models for barrier analysis—are highly relevant for modeling high-frequency limit order book data or calibrating complex derivatives pricing models (beyond the scope of the simple Black-Scholes template provided). Significant adaptation is required to shift focus from biological degradation to market risk/pricing.
title_cn: 带脉冲的布朗运动：扩散、桥、函数主成分分析和首次穿越模型在生物统计学中的指南
summary_cn: 该教程深入探讨了连续时间随机过程的数学工具，如SDE和函数PCA。虽然主要面向生物统计学，但其关于扩散过程、布朗桥和首次穿越时间分析的方法论对于处理高频市场微观结构数据、期权定价中的路径依赖性以及稀疏观测时间点下的时间序列插值具有潜在价值。需要将生物过程替换为金融时间序列。

title: Associative Memory for Non-Stationary Environments: A Self-Sizing Generalization of Hopfield Networks
summary: The Hopfield network made associative memory (AM) the model system of neural computation, but it solves the problem only for a \emph{stationary} world: a fixed set of memories, stored once into frozen weights. Real environments are non-stationary (e.g., memories arrive over time, drift, recur, and must be told apart from noise), where the classical formulation fails by catastrophic interference (the palimpsest problem) and by a capacity fixed in advance. We argue that this is not a peripheral limitation but the crux: under non-stationarity, memory and learning cease to be separate problems, and \emph{adaptation}, rather than one-shot optimization, becomes the operative capacity. We give a fresh formulation of the AM problem for non-stationary environments and a \emph{self-sizing} continual associative memory that generalizes Hopfield's: it stores new memories without erasing old ones (no forgetting), re-binds drifting and recurring memories, allocates a genuinely new memory only for true novelty, and grows its store to the environment's \emph{intrinsic} memory demand and no further. We rigorously show that this demand is the Urysohn width of the problem and can be estimated from data via a contrastive-similarity (CS) operator. The memory's size converges to this capacity online with no preset value and no validation search, matching an oracle capacity search. We use experiments with synthetic datasets to show that the generalization buys self-sizing and retention under non-stationarity, \emph{not} higher per-item recall fidelity, on which it matches strong baselines.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a generalized, self-sizing continual associative memory system that extends Hopfield networks to handle non-stationary environments. Key features include robust storage against catastrophic interference, adaptation to drifting memories, and dynamic sizing based on the intrinsic complexity (Urysohn width) of the data stream, estimated via a contrastive-similarity (CS) operator.
data_sources: Synthetic datasets are used for demonstration, but the methodology is designed for temporal sequences or patterns that change over time, which in finance translates to time-series data or sequences of market states.
alpha_potential: The methodology addresses the critical challenge in financial modeling: non-stationarity and concept drift. Traditional models suffer performance degradation when market regimes shift. This continual learning framework could be applied to: 1) Identifying and tracking evolving market regimes by treating regimes as 'memories.' 2) Building robust, adaptive pattern recognition systems for detecting complex, sequential market signals that adapt as the underlying market structure changes, leading to more persistent alpha generation than static models.
title_cn: 非平稳环境下的联想记忆：霍普菲尔德网络的自适应尺寸泛化
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种适应不断变化市场环境的自适应联想记忆模型，解决了传统模型在市场非平稳性下的灾难性遗忘问题。该方法能持续学习、识别和适应漂移的市场模式，并根据环境内在复杂度动态调整其容量。这为构建能长期有效识别和利用市场结构变化（如动态因子或交易信号）的鲁棒算法交易系统提供了新的思路。

title: Robust and Differentially Private Principal Component Analysis
summary: Recent advances have sparked significant interest in the development of privacy-preserving Principal Component Analysis (PCA). However, many existing approaches rely on restrictive assumptions, such as assuming sub-Gaussian data or being vulnerable to data contamination. Additionally, some methods are computationally expensive or depend on unknown model parameters that must be estimated, limiting their accessibility for data analysts seeking privacy-preserving PCA. In this paper, we propose a differentially private PCA method applicable to heavy-tailed and potentially contaminated data. Our approach leverages the property that the covariance matrix of properly rescaled data preserves eigenvectors and their order under elliptical distributions, which include Gaussian and heavy-tailed distributions. By applying a bounded transformation, we enable straightforward computation of principal components in a differentially private manner. Additionally, boundedness guarantees robustness against data contamination. We conduct both theoretical analysis and empirical evaluations of the proposed method, focusing on its ability to recover the subspace spanned by the leading principal components. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms existing approaches in terms of statistical utility, particularly in non-Gaussian or contaminated data settings.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a robust, differentially private Principal Component Analysis (PCA) method utilizing bounded transformations on properly rescaled data. This approach ensures the preservation of eigenvectors and their order even when data is heavy-tailed or contaminated, enabling reliable PCA calculation under privacy constraints.
data_sources: General financial datasets where PCA is applied, especially those that might exhibit heavy-tailed distributions (common in financial returns) or suffer from potential data contamination (e.g., adversarial attacks or erroneous data points). This could apply to time-series market data or cross-sectional factor data.
alpha_potential: While the primary focus is privacy preservation and robustness, the ability to perform accurate PCA on noisy, heavy-tailed financial data is crucial for factor modeling and portfolio optimization. Robust PCA can reduce the sensitivity of factor exposures to outliers, leading to more stable and reliable factor-based strategies (e.g., risk parity, low-volatility portfolios, or multi-factor screening). The differential privacy aspect is particularly relevant for firms sharing aggregated model outputs or using proprietary data sensitive to inference attacks.
title_cn: 稳健且差分隐私的奇异值分解（PCA）
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种适用于重尾和受污染金融数据的稳健且差分隐私的PCA方法。在构建因子模型或投资组合优化时，该技术能提供对异常值更强的鲁棒性，同时保护底层数据隐私。这有助于开发更稳定、更安全的量化策略，尤其是在高频或敏感数据场景下进行特征提取和降维。

title: High-Dimensional Differentially Private Quantile Regression: Distributed Estimation and Statistical Inference
summary: With the development of big data and machine learning, privacy concerns have become increasingly critical, especially when handling heterogeneous datasets containing sensitive personal information. Differential privacy provides a rigorous framework for safeguarding individual privacy while enabling meaningful statistical analysis. In this paper, we propose a differentially private quantile regression method for high-dimensional data in a distributed setting. Quantile regression is a powerful and robust tool for modeling the relationships between the covariates and responses in the presence of outliers or heavy-tailed distributions. To address the computational challenges due to the non-smoothness of the quantile loss function, we introduce a Newton-type transformation that reformulates the quantile regression task into an ordinary least squares problem. Building on this, we develop a differentially private estimation algorithm with iterative updates, ensuring both near-optimal statistical accuracy and formal privacy guarantees. For inference, we further propose a differentially private debiased estimator, which enables valid confidence interval construction and hypothesis testing. Additionally, we propose a communication-efficient and differentially private bootstrap for simultaneous hypothesis testing in high-dimensional quantile regression, suitable for distributed settings with both small and abundant local data. Extensive simulations demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of our methods in practical scenarios.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a differentially private method for high-dimensional quantile regression in a distributed setting. Key techniques include a Newton-type transformation to convert the non-smooth quantile regression loss into an ordinary least squares problem, enabling iterative updates with formal privacy guarantees. It also introduces a differentially private debiased estimator and a communication-efficient bootstrap for hypothesis testing.
data_sources: The methods are designed for high-dimensional, heterogeneous datasets potentially containing sensitive personal information, implying use cases involving financial transaction data, proprietary client data, or potentially high-dimensional alternative datasets where privacy is paramount.
alpha_potential: While not directly proposing an alpha signal, the methodology enables robust risk management and prediction in sensitive settings. Quantile regression is crucial for modeling tail risk (Value-at-Risk, Expected Shortfall) and constructing robust portfolio hedging strategies. Differential privacy allows proprietary financial firms to use highly sensitive internal data for model training (e.g., high-frequency trade patterns or client behavior) while maintaining data privacy compliance, thus unlocking proprietary alpha sources that were previously unusable due to privacy constraints.
title_cn: 高维差分隐私分位数回归：分布式估计与统计推断
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种用于高维和分布式数据的差分隐私分位数回归方法。核心在于通过牛顿型变换将非光滑的损失函数转化为最小二乘问题，从而实现隐私保护下的高效估计和有效统计推断。在量化金融中，该技术可用于在保护敏感交易或客户数据隐私的前提下，稳健地进行尾部风险（如VaR/ES）建模和构建受隐私约束的投资组合优化策略。

title: Adam symmetry theorem: characterization of the convergence of the stochastic Adam optimizer
summary: Beside the standard stochastic gradient descent (SGD) method, the Adam optimizer due to Kingma & Ba (2014) is currently probably the best-known optimization method for the training of deep neural networks in artificial intelligence (AI) systems. Despite the popularity and the success of Adam it remains an \emph{open research problem} to provide a rigorous convergence analysis for Adam even for the class of strongly convex SOPs. In one of the main results of this work we establish convergence rates for Adam in terms of the number of gradient steps (convergence rate \nicefrac{1}{2} w.r.t. the size of the learning rate), the size of the mini-batches (convergence rate 1 w.r.t. the size of the mini-batches), and the size of the second moment parameter of Adam (convergence rate 1 w.r.t. the distance of the second moment parameter to 1) for the class of strongly convex SOPs. In a further main result of this work, which we refer to as \emph{Adam symmetry theorem}, we illustrate the optimality of the established convergence rates by proving for a special class of simple quadratic strongly convex SOPs that Adam converges as the number of gradient steps increases to infinity to the solution of the SOP (the unique minimizer of the strongly convex objective function) if and \emph{only} if the random variables in the SOP (the data in the SOP) are \emph{symmetrically distributed}. In particular, in the standard case where the random variables in the SOP are not symmetrically distributed we \emph{disprove} that Adam converges to the minimizer of the SOP as the number of Adam steps increases to infinity. We also complement the conclusions of our convergence analysis and the Adam symmetry theorem by several numerical simulations that indicate the sharpness of the established convergence rates and that illustrate the practical appearance of the phenomena revealed in the \emph{Adam symmetry theorem}.
core_methodology: The paper rigorously analyzes the convergence properties of the Adam optimizer, particularly establishing convergence rates for strongly convex stochastic optimization problems (SOPs). The 'Adam symmetry theorem' demonstrates that convergence to the true minimizer only occurs if the underlying random variables (data) are symmetrically distributed; otherwise, it diverges in the limit.
data_sources: The research uses theoretical stochastic optimization problems (SOPs), which in finance often represent objective functions derived from trading signals, portfolio selection, or model calibration tasks involving noisy market data.
alpha_potential: This research has high relevance for any quantitative strategy that utilizes deep learning optimization techniques, especially when training models (like Reinforcement Learning agents or predictive networks) on noisy, potentially non-symmetrically distributed financial time series data. If a trading model is optimized using Adam and the underlying data generating process does not meet the symmetry condition, the optimization process might fail to converge to the best parameters, leading to suboptimal trading decisions or lack of profitability. Understanding these limitations allows researchers to select more robust optimizers or adapt objectives/data distributions.
title_cn: Adam对称性定理：随机Adam优化器收敛性的表征
summary_cn: 该论文深入分析了Adam优化器的收敛性，特别是证明了在应用于金融数据时，Adam仅当随机变量（数据）对称分布时才能收敛到最优解。对于许多具有非对称噪声的市场数据，这表明Adam优化可能收敛到次优参数，直接影响深度学习交易模型的性能和稳定性。研究者应警惕Adam在处理金融数据时的潜在失效风险。

title: Non-Euclidean SGD for Structured Optimization: Unified Analysis and Improved Rates
summary: Recently, several instances of non-Euclidean SGD, including SignSGD, Lion, and Muon, have attracted significant interest from the optimization community due to their practical success in training deep neural networks. Consequently, a number of works have attempted to explain this success by developing theoretical convergence analyses. Unfortunately, these results cannot properly justify the superior performance of these methods, as they could not beat the convergence rate of vanilla Euclidean SGD. We resolve this important open problem by developing a new unified convergence analysis under the structured smoothness and gradient noise assumption. In particular, our results indicate that non-Euclidean SGD (i) can exploit the sparsity or low-rank structure of the upper bounds on the Hessian and gradient noise, (ii) can provably benefit from popular algorithmic tools such as extrapolation or momentum variance reduction, and (iii) can match the state-of-the-art convergence rates of adaptive and more complex optimization algorithms such as AdaGrad and Shampoo.
core_methodology: This paper develops a unified theoretical convergence analysis for non-Euclidean Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) methods (like SignSGD, Lion, Muon). It establishes that these methods can achieve state-of-the-art convergence rates, matching complex adaptive algorithms like AdaGrad or Shampoo, especially when exploiting underlying structural properties (smoothness, noise structure) of the optimization landscape. The key technical advance is resolving the open problem where previous analyses could not beat standard Euclidean SGD rates.
data_sources: The analysis focuses on the optimization process itself, applicable to training any complex machine learning model on financial data (e.g., time series, order book data, fundamental data).
alpha_potential: While not presenting a direct alpha signal, this research drastically improves the efficiency and theoretical guarantees of training sophisticated models common in advanced quantitative finance, such as deep reinforcement learning agents for optimal trade execution, or large Transformer models for high-frequency market prediction. Improved convergence rates mean models can be trained faster and potentially find better optima on complex, non-convex financial objective functions, leading to more robust and profitable trading policies.
title_cn: 非欧几里得随机梯度下降的结构化优化：统一分析与改进收敛率
summary_cn: 该研究为Lion、SignSGD等非欧几里得SGD算法提供了统一的收敛性理论分析，证明它们在特定结构下可匹配AdaGrad等复杂优化器的性能。这对于高效训练应用于金融市场的深度学习模型（如强化学习执行算法或高频预测模型）至关重要，有助于更快、更稳定地找到最优交易策略解。

title: Universal priors: solving empirical Bayes via Bayesian inference and pretraining
summary: We theoretically justify the recent empirical finding of [Teh et al., 2025] that a transformer pretrained on synthetically generated data achieves strong performance on empirical Bayes (EB) problems. We take an indirect approach to this question: rather than analyzing the model architecture or training dynamics, we ask why a pretrained Bayes estimator, trained under a prespecified training distribution, can adapt to arbitrary test distributions. Focusing on Poisson EB problems, we identify the existence of universal priors such that training under these priors yields a near-optimal regret bound of $\widetilde{O}(\frac{1}{n})$ uniformly over all test distributions. Our analysis leverages the classical phenomenon of posterior contraction in Bayesian statistics, showing that the pretrained transformer adapts to unknown test distributions precisely through posterior contraction. This perspective also explains the phenomenon of length generalization, in which the test sequence length exceeds the training length, as the model performs Bayesian inference using a generalized posterior.
core_methodology: The research analyzes why transformers pretrained on synthetic data generalize well to unseen empirical Bayes (EB) problems. The core insight revolves around 'universal priors' and the mechanism of posterior contraction in Bayesian statistics, specifically showing how a pretrained Bayes estimator adapts to unknown test distributions via this contraction.
data_sources: The analysis focuses on Poisson Empirical Bayes problems. While the paper uses synthetic data for training justification, the implications relate to inferring unknown data distributions (test distributions), which, in finance, could involve time-series dynamics, volatility estimation, or risk assessment based on observed market data.
alpha_potential: This work offers a theoretical underpinning for using large, pretrained models (Transformers) in complex statistical inference tasks common in quantitative finance, such as superior parameter estimation in high-dimensional settings or robust prediction under distribution shift. The finding that pretrained models can adapt optimally ($O(1/n)$ regret) signals a pathway to building robust, adaptive estimators for financial signals (like dynamic volatility or non-stationary asset returns) that traditionally suffer from reliance on specific distribution assumptions.
title_cn: 通用先验：通过贝叶斯推断和预训练解决经验贝叶斯问题
summary_cn: 该研究从理论上解释了预训练Transformer模型在经验贝叶斯问题上的泛化能力，核心在于“通用先验”和后验收缩机制。这为利用预训练大模型进行金融数据（如高维参数估计、非平稳资产回报率建模）的稳健推理提供了理论依据，有望提升策略对市场分布变化的适应性，从而增强模型鲁棒性。

title: Revisiting OmniAnomaly for Anomaly Detection: performance metrics and comparison with PCA-based models
summary: Deep learning models have become the dominant approach for multivariate time series anomaly detection (MTSAD), often reporting substantial performance improvements over classical statistical methods. However, these gains are frequently evaluated under heterogeneous thresholding strategies and evaluation protocols, making fair comparisons difficult. This work revisits OmniAnomaly, a widely used stochastic recurrent model for MTSAD, and systematically compares it with a simple linear baseline based on Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on the Server Machine Dataset (SMD). Both methods are evaluated under identical thresholding and evaluation procedures, with experiments repeated across 100 runs for each of the 28 machines in the dataset. Performance is evaluated using Precision, Recall and F1-score at point-level, with and without point-adjustment, and under different aggregation strategies across machines and runs, with the corresponding standard deviations also reported. The results show large variability across machines and show that PCA can achieve performance comparable to OmniAnomaly, and even outperform it when point-adjustment is not applied. These findings question the added value of more complex architectures under current benchmarking practices and highlight the critical role of evaluation methodology in MTSAD research.
core_methodology: Revisiting OmniAnomaly (a stochastic recurrent deep learning model) and comparing it systematically against a Principal Component Analysis (PCA)-based linear baseline for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection (MTSAD). The core focus is on rigorous evaluation protocols, including identical thresholding and robust statistical reporting (F1-score, Precision, Recall).
data_sources: Server Machine Dataset (SMD), containing multivariate time series data from server monitoring.
alpha_potential: While this study focuses on machine monitoring anomalies (industrial IoT context), the core finding—that simple linear models (PCA) can match or outperform complex deep learning models (OmniAnomaly) when evaluation metrics are controlled—is highly relevant to quantitative finance. It suggests that simpler anomaly detection or regime change models based on variance/covariance analysis (like PCA) might be sufficient and more robust than complex deep generative models when benchmarking for trading signals. This challenges the need for deep learning complexity in creating robust market regime detection signals.
title_cn: 重新审视 OmniAnomaly 用于异常检测：性能指标与基于 PCA 模型的比较
